diagnosis: Rollout 3 (rollout_index=3) is the sole failing rollout and it auto-failed on the turn cap at turn_count=12 with no settlement, no revealed_facts, and empty content/provenance results. The failure is structural, not a content-check failure: A2 (owner of PF1) attempted to reveal PF1 at turn 3 but produced an unparsable model output (raw_output: `{"type":" "}"reveal", ...`), which the harness recorded as a 'say' event rather than a 'reveal'. A2 attempted again at turn 8 with another unparsable output (raw_output: `{"type":" "say", "text": ...}`). At turn 11, A2 finally produced a valid 'say' event containing the full substance of PF1 (dedicated speech-generating device, TouchChat, 20 minutes daily), but because it was a 'say' rather than a 'reveal' action, the fact was never registered as revealed. Meanwhile, A3 (owner of PF2) never got a turn to reveal PF2 because A1 rigidly enforced an agenda ordering requiring A2's report before A3's, and A1 kept waiting for A2 to successfully produce a formatted reveal. The turn cap was consumed by repeated retries and procedural back-and-forth. Because no facts were ever revealed via a 'reveal' action, the settle-eligibility condition (which presumably requires both PF1 and PF2 to be revealed) never triggered, and the group hit the 12-turn cap. This is a structural problem: a single malformed JSON output from one agent cascaded into a full failure because the settle-eligibility condition and the agenda ordering prevented the other fact-holder from revealing independently. The turn cap of 12 was not inherently too low — rollouts 0, 1, and 2 all settled within 4-6 turns — but the rigid ordering and the inability to recover from a parse error consumed all 12 turns without either fact being formally revealed. No content checks (C1-C8) or provenance check P1 failed in any settled rollout; all failures are confined to this single auto-failed rollout where no checks were evaluated at all.
